questions.q: What mistake does the story of Nasreddin and the lost key illustrate?
a: Searching for happiness outside because it feels easier
Looking for a lost object in the wrong house
Trusting strangers with deeply personal problems
Refusing help when it is kindly offered
questions.why: Russell uses the story to show that we hunt for happiness outside ourselves because the outer world feels familiar.

questions.q: Why is letting go so difficult, according to Russell?
a: We treat it as another task instead of stopping the holding on
We lack the discipline to finish what we start
We are surrounded by people who hold grudges
We forget the original cause of our pain
questions.why: The first lesson says letting go cannot be forced by effort; we must stop clinging instead.

questions.q: What are the two steps of the letting-go practice?
a: Letting in and letting be
Noticing and naming
Accepting and forgetting
Breathing and relaxing
questions.why: The second lesson says the practice consists of letting in the experience and then letting it be without trying to change it.

questions.q: What does it mean to let in a painful experience?
a: Turn toward it with curiosity and observe the sensation
Distract yourself until the feeling passes
Explain to someone why the pain is unfair
Replace the painful thought with a happier one
questions.why: Russell suggests tilting your head just enough to tolerate the pain, then getting curious about what the sensation is like.

questions.q: According to Russell, what always comes along with an emotion?
a: A story about the past or the future
A physical illness or chronic tension
A desire to change other people
A memory from early childhood
questions.why: The third lesson says every emotion comes with a story, and you cannot feel the emotion without telling yourself that story.
